Synopsis

India's pharmaceutical exports could reach USD 32-33 billion in FY27, growing 5-6%, as the country offsets weaker shipments to the US by expanding into Latin America, Africa and ASEAN markets, Pharmexcil Director General K Raja Bhanu said. Supply chain diversification has also helped the sector navigate geopolitical disruptions.

Listen to this article in summarized format

Exports of pharmaceutical products from India are growing at 5-6 per cent currently and could reach USD 32-33 billion in the ongoing financial year, a senior official said on Monday.

Speaking to the media on the sidelines of CPHI India 2026, Pharmexcil Director General K Raja Bhanu said, "Pharma exports from India have crossed USD 30 billion, and we are growing about 5-6 per cent... looking at that, we may reach about USD 32-33 billion this financial year."

He admitted that pharma exports to the US saw a dip, but pointed out that India has been exploring new markets and "we are fairly hitting it up in Latin America, Africa, and ASEAN nations".

This year saw multiple supply chain disruptions arising out of geopolitical conflicts, but the country has been able to negate the adverse impact through supply chain diversification.

"We were able to overcome that by importing from some other countries," he said. The Pharmaceuticals Export Promotion Council of India (Pharexcil) is the apex government agency for the promotion of pharmaceutical exports.

Sharing some key statistics, Informa Markets Managing Director Yogesh Mudras said India's pharmaceutical industry continues to demonstrate strong manufacturing momentum, with annual turnover reaching Rs 5.08 lakh crore in FY26, registering an average growth of 9.2 per cent over the preceding five years. Alongside this, domestic manufacturing of medical devices expanded approximately 48.2 per cent, increasing from Rs 28,000 crore in FY20 to Rs 41,500 crore in FY25.

"The next phase of growth will depend on moving towards high-value segments such as advanced biologics, specialised therapies and complex formulations, supported by investments in advanced manufacturing infrastructure and technology... Through this event, we aim to support innovation and strengthen India's position in the global pharmaceutical ecosystem," he said.

The three-day CPHI India 2026 - one of the country's premier pharmaceutical industry exhibitions - started at IICC, Yashobhoomi, in the national capital on Monday.

This year's edition introduces an expanded two-venue format, with CPHI India taking place from November 23-25 at IICC, Yashobhoomi, and PMEC India scheduled from November 24-26 at India Expo Mart Ltd (IEML), Greater Noida.

Together, the co-located exhibitions bring the pharmaceutical ecosystem onto a common platform, connecting stakeholders across ingredients, formulations, processing machinery, packaging and manufacturing technologies, Informa Markets, one of the organisers of the event, said in a statement.

The combined platform features over 2,000 exhibitors and is expected to attract 50,000 visitors from more than 120 countries over the next few days.

Federation of Pharma Entrepreneurs (FOPE) National President Harish K Jain; Joint Drug Controller India, CDSCO, Chandrashekar Ranga; Director General, Organisation of Pharmaceutical Producers of India (OPPI) Anil Matai, among others, spoke during the inauguration of the event.
